subject.title: feat(cron): shell precheck gate to skip LLM when no work

question: Should a cron precheck be permitted to execute arbitrary Gateway-host shell commands for every cron writer, or must it reuse the existing governed exec/trigger authorization and sandbox policy?
rationale: The PR intentionally introduces a new unattended command path while bypassing the trigger enablement gate; choosing its permanent authorization model is a security and product-boundary decision, not a mechanical refactor.

options.title: Reuse governed execution policy
options.body: Require the precheck runner to use the existing scheduled-exec authorization, approval, and sandbox policy, with focused tests for denied and allowed jobs.

options.title: Adopt a separate cron-exec policy
options.body: Define and document a distinct cron precheck permission model, including which Gateway callers may create these jobs and how existing installations opt in.

options.title: Defer host-shell prechecks
options.body: Keep the existing trigger and command/script approaches until the cron authorization model is explicitly designed.

recommendation.title: Reuse governed execution policy
recommendation.body: Require the precheck runner to use the existing scheduled-exec authorization, approval, and sandbox policy, with focused tests for denied and allowed jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence project-level routing candidate; the available evidence does not establish a more specific current-main cron security owner.
